subsystems.name: Reprogramming payload
subsystems.role: transiently switches on a small set of transcription factors that reset the epigenetic marks of an aged cell.
parts: Yamanaka-factor genes (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4) or their mRNA
regulatory elements that switch expression on and off
stabilising chemistry for the RNA or DNA

subsystems.name: Delivery vehicle
subsystems.role: gets the payload into cells of a chosen tissue without reaching the rest of the body.

subsystems.name: Dose and duration control
subsystems.role: keeps reprogramming partial — enough to rejuvenate, not enough to make cells pluripotent.

subsystems.name: Safety and tumour surveillance
subsystems.role: catches cells that escape control before they grow into tumours.

subsystems.name: Measurement and biomarkers
subsystems.role: tells researchers whether biological age actually moved.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing and quality control
subsystems.role: produces a consistent biologic product for testing.

buildSteps.title: Choose the target
buildSteps.detail: Pick one accessible tissue and one measurable condition — eye, skin, muscle or liver — so a change can be observed directly.

buildSteps.title: Prove partial reprogramming in cells
buildSteps.detail: Cells from aged donors are treated briefly with the factors and checked for reversed epigenetic marks without losing their identity.

buildSteps.title: Show benefit in animals
buildSteps.detail: Mice engineered to express the factors on demand are used to test whether short bursts improve tissue function and extend healthy life.

buildSteps.title: Design the human payload
buildSteps.detail: The factor set, its control elements and the expression window are tuned for human cells, usually dropping the oncogenic c-Myc factor.

buildSteps.title: Build the delivery route
buildSteps.detail: Lipid nanoparticles or viral vectors are engineered to reach only the target tissue after a local or intravenous dose.

buildSteps.title: Test safety before humans
buildSteps.detail: Long-term animal studies check for tumours, immune reactions and off-target expression at many times the intended dose.

buildSteps.title: Run first-in-human safety studies
buildSteps.detail: A small trial in patients with one condition measures tolerability, where the payload ended up, and early functional change.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a therapy
buildSteps.detail: If safe, larger trials test whether the treatment changes the course of a specific age-related disease, with manufacturing scaled to match.

prerequisites.why: discovered in 2006 and recognised with the 2012 Nobel Prize in Medicine; the core biology is well established in cells and mice.

prerequisites.tech: In vivo delivery of RNA or gene therapy
prerequisites.why: lipid nanoparticles and viral vectors are already used in approved medicines, so a vehicle exists to borrow.
DNA-methylation clocks track age in populations but are not yet accepted as proof that a treatment worked in one patient.
keeping the factors on for days rather than weeks, and only in one organ, is the difference between rejuvenation and cancer.
regulators approve treatments for named diseases, not for ageing itself, so a specific condition must be chosen and measured.

pathway.milestone: research groups and companies such as Altos Labs, founded in 2022, run cell and animal reprogramming experiments
pathway.unlocks: a map of which factors, doses and tissues produce benefit without harm.

pathway.milestone: first-in-human safety trials in a single accessible tissue, most likely the eye
pathway.unlocks: evidence that partial reprogramming is tolerable in people.

pathway.milestone: trials that show functional improvement in one age-related disease
pathway.unlocks: a regulatory route, since success in one disease opens the door to others.

pathway.milestone: combination regimens pairing reprogramming with other ageing-targeted drugs
pathway.unlocks: broader healthspan extension, if long-term cancer risk stays controlled.
a shift from treating disease to delaying it — the hardest thing to prove or approve.
